items.stem: A system that always applies "if X, then Y" written by people is mainly:
Learned behavior in AI mainly comes from:

options.A: One engineer typing every possible case by hand
options.B: Patterns found in many examples during the practice phase

items.stem: Which is the clearest rules-based example?

options.A: "If the badge is valid, unlock the door"
options.B: A feed that slowly matches your taste
options.C: A tool that invents new song styles from millions of tracks

items.stem: Which is the clearest learned-behavior example?

options.B: A thermostat fixed at one number
options.C: A spam filter improving after many labeled emails

items.stem: Why might a pure rule system fail on a new case?

options.B: Nobody wrote a rule that covers that case
options.C: It refuses to follow instructions on purpose

items.stem: Why might a learned system make a strange mistake?

options.A: It copied a weak or biased pattern from its examples

items.stem: "The know-how the AI has learned from examples" is built mainly by:

options.A: Printing a paper manual each morning
options.C: Practice on many examples, then using those patterns later

items.stem: A checkout rule "discount 10% on Tuesdays" is best described as:

options.C: An AI inventing prices each hour

items.stem: When should you suspect learned behavior rather than simple rules?

options.A: The tool improves after seeing more labeled examples
options.B: The output never changes for any input
options.C: A person rewrites one clear if-then line
